findings.evidence: R7 requires documentation/examples.md to have three recipes: (1) an icon-only button with aria-label, (2) overriding a default icon, (3) using the icon in a custom control. Recipe 7 ("Reusing the Standard Icons", lines 332-358) contains only (1) at lines 347-351 and (3) at line 353. There is no example that keeps a built-in semanticType and replaces its built-in icon. Recipe 4's only built-in override (lines 196-199) changes delete.buttonStyle, and documentation/configuration.md:181-194 overrides delete.buttonStyle and confirmOptions only; neither touches visualOptions.iconLeft/iconRight. A search for semanticType together with iconLeft/iconRight across README.md and documentation/*.md returns no match, so the capability is not shown anywhere. architect-r1 also lists "overriding a built-in icon" among the documentation deliverables for this feature.
findings.description: The examples page is missing one of the three recipes R7 names explicitly, so readers are never shown how to replace a built-in type's default icon. Add a short recipe, e.g. `<ZestButton zest={{ semanticType: 'save', visualOptions: { iconLeft: <ZestIcon name="archive" /> } }}>Archive</ZestButton>` (and/or the provider form `semanticTypeDefaults: { save: { visualOptions: { iconLeft: <ZestIcon name="archive" /> } } }`), with the default import of ZestButton and a named ZestIcon import.

findings.evidence: The documented provider configuration does not type-check: when the `const appZestConfig = { semanticTypeDefaults: { delete: { buttonStyle: 'outline', ... } } }` snippet (examples.md:183-200, identical shape at configuration.md:181-197) is checked with `npx tsc --noEmit --strict`, `buttonStyle` widens to `string` and `<ZestButtonConfigProvider config={appZestConfig}>` fails with TS2322: `Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'ZestButtonStyle | undefined'`. Passing the object inline or annotating it as `ZestGlobalConfig` (or `as const`) fixes it. The pattern predates this change (it is present at 126a067), so this is advisory rather than a regression.
findings.description: R7's acceptance says every documented example must compile against the real types. The override examples are pre-existing, but they are still part of the pages this feature rewrites and they currently show TypeScript an error. Annotate the config objects (`const appZestConfig: ZestGlobalConfig = ...`) or inline them so the recipes compile.

findings.evidence: Lines 518-520 are indented four spaces while the surrounding statements inside the same `it(...)` block are indented six, e.g. `    expect(read("README.md")).toContain("toggleOptions");` sits under a block whose other statements start at column seven. The mis-indentation was introduced with the version-expectation update from 1.6.0 to 1.7.0; it is cosmetic and does not affect behaviour.
findings.description: Restore the original indentation so the diff only changes the version values.
